title: Mutable Defaults
prompt_markdown: Why is it dangerous to use a mutable object like a list as a default argument value?

content.reference_answer: Default arguments are evaluated only once at function definition time. If a mutable object is used, the same object is shared across all calls that use the default, leading to unexpected behavior.
A pure function always returns the same output for the same input and has no observable side effects (like modifying global state or performing I/O).
